hero.headline: Trump to press Netanyahu against retaliating for Iranian missile attack
hero.body:
President Trump said he will call Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to urge him not to retaliate after Iran launched ballistic missiles at northern Israel on Sunday, threatening a ceasefire the administration has worked to broker. Trump told Axios he would press Netanyahu to stand down, saying both sides have now struck each other and further escalation is unnecessary.

The Iranian attack marked the first such strike in two months and came after Israel struck Beirut earlier. The Israeli Defense Forces confirmed multiple waves of ballistic missiles were fired at northern Israel. A U.S. official told NewsNation that Trump has been briefed on the incident. The attack raised immediate concerns about the fragility of the ceasefire arrangement between the United States and Iran.

Trump framed the situation as a cycle both countries need to end. He told Axios that Israel had conducted its strike and Iran had now responded, characterizing the exchanges as both sides having their opportunity to act. The president indicated he sees no need for another round of attacks and hopes to preserve prospects for a lasting peace deal in the region.

The strikes threaten to derail ongoing efforts to negotiate a broader agreement aimed at ending the conflict. Diplomats have worked for weeks to establish terms that could hold, but the Sunday night attack underscored how quickly tensions can reignite. The timing comes as the Trump administration approaches the 18-month mark of its second term, with Middle East policy remaining a central focus.

Former national security adviser John Bolton warned separately that Trump's handling of the Iran situation could trigger nuclear proliferation in the Middle East. Bolton wrote in an opinion piece that contradictory decisions during the conflict have created conditions for a potential arms race, regardless of whatever deal the administration ultimately reaches with Tehran. The administration now faces the immediate task of preventing further escalation while trying to keep diplomatic channels open.

cards.headline: OPEC+ Increases Oil Output Quota as Strait of Hormuz Remains Closed
cards.teaser: The oil cartel approved a fourth production increase since the closure of the critical shipping route, though most of the output remains stranded.
cards.body:
OPEC+ has approved an increase in oil production quotas by 188,000 barrels per day, marking the fourth such hike since the effective shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz. The move comes as the cartel attempts to address global supply constraints caused by the ongoing Iran conflict.

The production increase is largely symbolic given that vast amounts of the world's oil remain stranded due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a critical chokepoint for global petroleum exports. The ceasefire in Iran remains elusive, leaving the strategic waterway inaccessible and limiting the practical impact of increased production quotas on actual oil delivery to global markets.

cards.headline: Stock Market Erases $1.4 Trillion After Strong Jobs Report Raises Rate Hike Concerns
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 suffered its worst day of the year as investors fled technology and AI stocks on fears of Federal Reserve interest rate increases.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 fell 2.6 percent while the Nasdaq dropped 4 percent—its worst day in over a year—after the U.S. added 172,000 jobs in May. The stronger-than-expected employment figures raised concerns about potential Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, prompting investors to sell off technology and semiconductor stocks.

The resilient labor market stood in contrast to broader economic concerns, including rising inflation and uncertainty from Middle East conflict. The market selloff reflected traders reassessing valuations as they weighed robust employment data against the possibility of tighter monetary policy ahead.

cards.headline: Trump Calls for Rate Cut as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Prepares to Take Office
cards.teaser: The president criticized potential interest rate increases ahead of the new Federal Reserve chairman's debut, saying there is no reason to raise rates.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump has publicly urged the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates, adding pressure on incoming chair Kevin Warsh as he prepares to assume leadership of the central bank. Trump said there is no reason to raise interest rates following the latest jobs report, despite market expectations moving in the opposite direction.

The president expressed surprise at stock market declines that followed the strong employment data. Barclays analysts warned that markets are entering a warning zone as traders recalibrate expectations for monetary policy. Trump stated that the Fed chair should do whatever he wants but made clear his opposition to rate hikes at this time.

cards.headline: Senate passes immigration enforcement funding bill
cards.teaser: The Senate approved major immigration enforcement funding legislation, sending the measure to the House for consideration.
cards.body:
The Senate passed a significant immigration enforcement funding bill, marking progress for Trump administration deportation priorities. The legislation now moves to the House of Representatives for consideration.

Lawmakers face additional immigration-related decisions in the coming days, including the future of a surveillance program set to expire next week. The bill represents a victory for the administration's enforcement agenda, though further legislative battles loom.

cards.headline: Zelensky Meets European Allies in London as U.S. Focus Shifts to Iran
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to London to meet with leaders of Britain, Germany, and France as the United States steps back from mediation efforts.
cards.body:
Zelensky met with British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, French President Emmanuel Macron, and German opposition leader Friedrich Merz in London on Sunday to discuss Ukraine's defense needs and potential peace negotiations. The gathering took place hours after Russia fired hypersonic weapons and drones at Ukraine, including a strike near the Chornobyl nuclear power plant.

The European leaders discussed the urgent need to strengthen Ukraine's air defenses and deep-strike capabilities. Ukraine's closest European allies set out five conditions for any future peace talks with Russia. The meeting underscored Europe's growing diplomatic role as the U.S. shifts its focus toward Iran.

cards.headline: U.S. Considers Using Frozen Iranian Assets to Aid Gulf Allies
cards.teaser: The Treasury Department is exploring plans to steer frozen Iranian assets toward reconstruction efforts in Gulf states allied with the United States.
cards.body:
Washington is considering using Iranian assets frozen under U.S. sanctions to help Gulf allies recover from damages. The proposal would redirect funds held in American-controlled accounts to assist partner nations in the Persian Gulf region with reconstruction costs.

Iran rejected the idea outright, according to reports. Iranian officials dismissed any suggestion that the country's assets could be used to pay damages to U.S. allies. The proposal comes as the broader conflict between the United States and Iran intensifies, with American officials seeking ways to support regional partners while maintaining economic pressure on Tehran.

cards.headline: Senegal's President and Prime Minister Locked in Public Feud
cards.teaser: The two men who defeated Senegal's political establishment together now find themselves in a bitter rift that is dividing the West African nation.
cards.body:
Senegal's president and prime minister, who rose to power as allies campaigning against the country's political old guard, are now engaged in a public conflict. The dispute between the two leaders threatens to destabilize the government they formed together after their electoral victory.

The rift has created divisions within Senegal's political landscape, with supporters and officials forced to choose sides between the two formerly united leaders. The nature of their disagreement and what triggered the split between the president and prime minister were not specified in available reports.

cards.headline: Iranian Public Faces Despair Amid War Deaths and Economic Crisis
cards.teaser: An imploding economy and mounting war casualties are causing widespread hopelessness across Iranian society, affecting both government supporters and opponents.
cards.body:
Iranians are experiencing deepening despair as the country faces both an economic collapse and rising death tolls from ongoing conflicts. Skyrocketing inflation has devastated household budgets and eroded purchasing power across the country, compounding the grief from military casualties.

The economic crisis is creating a sense of hopelessness that cuts across political lines, affecting both those who support the government and those who oppose it. For Iranians who had hoped recent turmoil might lead to regime change, the current situation has brought particular disappointment as conditions worsen without any apparent path toward political transformation.

cards.headline: Gunman Kills One in Attack in Central Israel
cards.teaser: An Arab citizen of Israel carried out a shooting attack that left one person dead before the assailant was killed.
cards.body:
A shooting attack in central Israel on Sunday claimed one life. The gunman, identified as an Arab citizen of Israel, was killed during the incident.

Hamas praised the attack but did not claim responsibility for it. The shooting underscores ongoing security tensions as Israel manages multiple concurrent conflicts, including strikes against Hezbollah in Lebanon and missile fire from Iran.

cards.headline: Rights Defender Works to Protect Ukrainian Soldiers From Own Military
cards.teaser: A human rights advocate in Ukraine focuses on protecting soldiers from abuses by their own commanders, not from Russian forces.
cards.body:
Ukraine has appointed a rights defender specifically charged with protecting the country's soldiers from mistreatment and abuses by their own military leadership. The position addresses internal military conduct issues rather than threats from Russian forces.

The role highlights concerns about conditions and treatment within Ukraine's armed forces as the war continues. The defender's work focuses on investigating complaints from soldiers about their commanders and ensuring accountability within the military hierarchy for violations of service members' rights.

cards.headline: Russian Strikes Kill Three in Ukraine During European Diplomatic Talks
cards.teaser: Russian attacks killed three people in Ukraine on the same day President Zelensky met with European leaders in London.
cards.body:
Russian strikes on Ukraine killed three people on Sunday, Ukrainian officials reported. The attacks occurred as President Volodymyr Zelensky met with European leaders in London, including the heads of Britain, Germany, and France, to discuss potential peace negotiations.

One strike hit near a nuclear site in Ukraine, though no radiation incidents were reported. During the meeting, Zelensky's European allies outlined five conditions for peace talks as discussions about the war's future continue in Western capitals.

hero.headline: 12 People Shot Near Festival in Toledo, Ohio
hero.body:
Twelve people were wounded in a shooting near the Old West End Festival in Toledo, Ohio on Saturday evening, with police continuing their search for at least two suspects on Sunday. Two victims remain in critical condition following the attack.

The gunfire erupted just after 5:30pm near the festival, an annual community event featuring live music and architectural home tours in the historic center of Toledo. According to Toledo police deputy chief Joseph Heffernan, the shooters were "probably shooting at each other" when the violence occurred. Several hundred people were attending the festival at the time.

The victims ranged in age from 14 to 61 years old, with most in their early 20s. No suspects had been taken into custody by Sunday as the investigation entered its second day. Law enforcement officials asked festival attendees to share any photos or videos from their phones that might provide leads in locating the shooters.

The shooting prompted festival organizers to cancel all planned Sunday events. In a statement, organizers expressed their heartbreak over the injuries and explained their decision to shut down the remainder of the festival. "We feel that it would not be compassionate, responsible or possible to continue the festival," they said, acknowledging that celebrations across the country have increasingly become targets for violence.

Police had assigned extra officers to the festival, and a significant number of off-duty officers were working as security for the event. Despite these precautions, the shooting still occurred. Fire chief Allison Armstrong noted that it was challenging to transport victims to area hospitals because roads were closed and traffic was congested as people fled the festival.

Deputy Chief Heffernan expressed frustration about the incident, saying it was unfortunate when individuals "decide to disrupt something that has been a beloved community event for many, many, many years."

Ohio governor Mike DeWine responded to the shooting with a statement expressing deep concern about the violence. "Summer festivals should be safe spaces for families to spend time together without fear of violence," DeWine said. Ohio senator Jon Husted also commented on the incident, calling the violence senseless and thanking law enforcement for their quick response and ongoing efforts to locate the suspects.

The Toledo shooting represents one of more than 170 mass shootings that have occurred in the United States so far this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines mass shootings as incidents in which four or more people are wounded or killed. The high frequency of such incidents has prompted repeated calls for stronger federal gun control measures, though Congress has not implemented substantial restrictions.

cards.headline: Nearly 11,000 Bottles of Bourbon Stolen From Philadelphia Warehouse
cards.teaser: Thieves stole nearly 11,000 bottles of bourbon worth approximately $500,000 from a warehouse in North Philadelphia.
cards.body:
The theft occurred at a warehouse in North Philadelphia during daylight hours. The stolen bourbon had an estimated value of approximately $500,000, making it one of the larger alcohol heists in recent memory.

Company officials confirmed the theft, though they have not released details about the specific brands or types of bourbon taken. Law enforcement is investigating the incident, but no arrests have been announced.

cards.headline: 3.6 Magnitude Earthquake Strikes East Bay Near Alamo
cards.teaser: A 3.6 magnitude earthquake shook the East Bay area of the San Francisco Bay region, followed by a smaller aftershock.
cards.body:
The earthquake struck near Alamo in the East Bay on Sunday morning, according to the United States Geological Survey. The temblor was followed by a smaller earthquake in the same area.

The USGS recorded the preliminary magnitude at 3.6. Earthquakes of this size can be felt by people in the affected area but typically cause minimal damage. No reports of injuries or significant structural damage have been issued.

cards.headline: Trump Ends NBC Interview After Dispute Over Election Claims
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump abruptly ended an interview with NBC after being challenged by host Kristen Welker over his claims about the 2020 election.
cards.body:
President Trump abruptly ended his appearance on NBC's Meet the Press after clashing with host Kristen Welker over his claims about the 2020 election being rigged. Welker repeatedly challenged Trump on the disputed assertions during the broadcast.

The confrontation prompted Trump to walk out of the interview, cutting short what was intended to be a longer segment that would have covered additional topics.

cards.headline: Birds in Cities Changing Songs to Compete With Traffic Noise
cards.teaser: Some birds living in urban areas are altering their songs to be heard over traffic and other city noise, according to new research.
cards.body:
Scientists at the Centre for Ecological Research in Hungary found that certain bird species are adapting their vocalizations in response to urban noise pollution. The research documents how birds modify their songs to compete with the sounds of traffic and other urban activity.

The findings add to a growing body of evidence showing how wildlife adapts to human-dominated environments. The study suggests that urban birds face acoustic challenges that their rural counterparts do not encounter, forcing evolutionary or behavioral changes in communication.

cards.headline: Israel Says Iran Launched Missile During Fragile Ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israel reported that Iran launched a missile at it, marking the first such attack since a ceasefire took effect in early April.
cards.body:
According to Israel, Iran launched a missile attack, marking the first direct Iranian strike since the ceasefire began in early April. The incident threatens to undermine ongoing mediation efforts to transform the temporary halt in fighting into a permanent agreement to end the conflict.

The attack complicates diplomatic initiatives that have been working to establish a lasting peace deal between the parties.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Beirut Suburbs in Response to Hezbollah Drone Attack
cards.teaser: Israel launched airstrikes on suburbs of Beirut in retaliation for a Hezbollah drone attack on Israeli military positions.
cards.body:
Israel launched retaliatory airstrikes on Beirut's suburbs after Hezbollah attacked Israeli military installations with fighter drones. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office confirmed the sequence of events and stated the strikes were ordered in response to Hezbollah's firing at Israeli territory.

The exchange marks an escalation in hostilities between Israel and the Lebanese militant group. The strikes occurred days after a US-brokered truce, potentially complicating ongoing mediation efforts.

cards.headline: Eli Lilly Diabetes Drug Shows Promise in Reducing Blood Sugar and Body Weight
cards.teaser: The pharmaceutical company's triple-action medication demonstrated effectiveness in treating obesity and related complications including sleep apnea and osteoarthritis pain.
cards.body:
Retatrutide, a new weekly injection for type 2 diabetes, has demonstrated significant benefits in clinical trials. Patients receiving the drug for 40 weeks lost more than four times as much weight as those given a placebo, while experiencing more than double the reduction in HbA1c, a measure of long-term blood sugar control.

The medication works differently from existing diabetes treatments by mimicking three gut hormones: GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon. While competitors like Ozempic and Mounjaro target one or two of these pathways, retatrutide's triple action also increases energy expenditure, offering a more comprehensive approach to managing both blood sugar and weight.

cards.headline: Comedy Film Takes $55 Million at Box Office in Biggest R-Rated Opening in 12 Years
cards.teaser: Scary Movie earned the largest opening weekend for an R-rated comedy in more than a decade.
cards.body:
The new Scary Movie film earned $55 million at the domestic box office over the weekend, marking the biggest opening for an R-rated comedy in 12 years. The film topped box office charts in the United States and Canada.

The strong performance demonstrates continued audience appetite for R-rated comedy content despite industry trends toward broader demographic appeal. The opening weekend numbers surpassed industry expectations and represented a significant milestone for the comedy genre in theatrical releases.

cards.headline: Appeals Court Allows Kars4Kids to Continue Broadcasting Ads in California
cards.teaser: A California appeals court reversed a lower court decision that found the charity's advertisements violated false-advertising laws.
cards.body:
Kars4Kids, the charity known for its distinctive jingle, can continue broadcasting its advertisements in California following an appeals court ruling. The decision overturned a lower court finding from last month that the ads violated false-advertising laws.

The appeals court ruling allows the charity to resume its advertising campaigns in the state. The legal dispute centered on claims about how the organization represents its charitable activities in its marketing materials.

cards.headline: Marks & Spencer Launches Training Program for 1,000 Young People
cards.teaser: The British retailer announced a new traineeship scheme aimed at young people not currently in employment, education, or training.
cards.body:
Marks & Spencer has launched a new traineeship program for 1,000 young people. The scheme is designed to address the growing challenge of youth unemployment and those not engaged in education or training.

The initiative represents M&S's commitment to tackling youth employment issues while supporting its own workforce development needs. By offering practical training opportunities, the retailer aims to help young people gain skills and enter the job market.

hero.headline: Atlantic Ocean current system shows signs of weakening, scientists warn
hero.body:
A new analysis has found that the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, a critical ocean current system, is far more likely to collapse than previously thought. The research combined real-world ocean observations with climate models to assess the future of the AMOC, producing findings that scientists have described as "very concerning."

The AMOC is a major component of the global climate system that transports warm tropical water to Europe and the Arctic, where it cools and sinks to form a deep return current. Previous studies had already shown the system is at its weakest point in 1,600 years due to climate change, but the new research narrows uncertainty about how much further it will weaken.

Climate scientists use dozens of computer models to predict future climate conditions, but for the complex AMOC system, these models produce widely varying results. Some suggest no further slowdown by 2100, while others predict a deceleration of about 65 percent. By comparing models with actual ocean observations, researchers found the most reliable predictions indicate a slowdown of 42 to 58 percent by 2100, a level almost certain to trigger collapse.

Dr Valentin Portmann, who led the research, stated: "We found that the Amoc is going to decline more than expected compared to the average of all climate models. This means we have an Amoc that is closer to a tipping point."

Professor Stefan Rahmstorf from the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research called the finding "an important and very concerning result." He explained: "The 'pessimistic' models, which show a strong weakening of the Amoc by 2100, are, unfortunately, the realistic ones, in that they agree better with observational data."

Rahmstorf, who has studied the AMOC for 35 years, expressed growing worry about reaching a shutdown tipping point by mid-century. When scientists previously thought the risk of collapse was about 5 percent, he said the risk was already too high given the potential impacts. "Now it looks like it's more than 50 percent," he added.

A collapse would have catastrophic consequences across multiple continents. Western Europe could experience extreme cold winters and summer droughts. The tropical rainfall belt that millions rely on for food production would shift. Sea levels around the Atlantic would rise by an additional 50 to 100 centimeters.

The AMOC is slowing because rapidly rising Arctic air temperatures cause ocean water to cool more slowly. Warmer water is less dense and sinks more slowly into the depths. This allows more rainfall to accumulate in surface waters, further reducing their density and creating a feedback loop that slows the circulation even more.

The research, published in the journal Science Advances, used a statistical method called ridge regression to identify which climate models best reflect observed ocean conditions, particularly surface salinity patterns in the south Atlantic.

cards.headline: Microsoft announces Xbox Series X 25th anniversary console in translucent green
cards.teaser: Microsoft is releasing a limited edition Xbox Series X in translucent green to mark the console brand's 25th anniversary.
cards.body:
Microsoft unveiled a limited edition Xbox Series X 25th Anniversary console featuring a translucent green design. The company is also releasing a matching controller in the same translucent green finish. Both items will be available in November.

The green color scheme references the original Xbox branding. The translucent design allows users to see internal components through the console's exterior. Microsoft positioned the release as a celebration of 25 years since the Xbox brand launched.

cards.headline: Notion restores access to Anthropic AI services after outage
cards.teaser: Notion has restored access to Anthropic AI features following a service disruption that affected users.
cards.body:
Notion experienced a temporary disruption to its AI services powered by Anthropic before restoring access. The outage affected users who rely on AI features integrated through Notion's partnership with Anthropic, which provides large language model capabilities.

Notion's head of product commented on the significant user response to the service interruption on social media, noting his surprise at how many people shared information about the outage.

cards.headline: Persona 6 announced for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC
cards.teaser: Atlus has officially announced Persona 6, confirming earlier leaks about the next installment in the role-playing game series.
cards.body:
Atlus officially confirmed Persona 6 during the Xbox Games Showcase, revealing the game will launch on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series consoles, and PC. The announcement came as part of this year's Summer Game Fest, which also featured the reveal of the Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy's conclusion.

The studio shared a brief teaser featuring a graveyard setting with a toxic green color scheme. Beyond these visuals, Atlus has kept details about gameplay and story under wraps for now.

cards.headline: Xbox announces return to console exclusives at 2026 Games Showcase
cards.teaser: Microsoft showcased multiple games that will be exclusive to Xbox and PC platforms, marking a shift in release strategy.
cards.body:
Microsoft held its 2026 Summer Xbox Games Showcase at Summer Game Fest, emphasizing exclusive titles for Xbox consoles and PC. The event featured world premieres and major game announcements across the company's gaming portfolio. Gears of War E-Day will launch October 6 as an Xbox and PC exclusive.

The showcase highlighted Microsoft's shift back toward platform exclusives after a period of multiplatform releases. The company also celebrated its 25th anniversary with special hardware, including a translucent green console and matching controller.

cards.headline: Halo: Campaign Evolved launches July 28 with new space combat missions
cards.teaser: The updated Halo game will include new space combat missions and is available for pre-order ahead of its July release.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced that Halo: Campaign Evolved will release on July 28 across Xbox Series S/X, PC, and PlayStation 5. The remake reimagines the original Halo: Combat Evolved campaign with new content.

The game introduces Operation: Meteorite, a fresh three-mission addition featuring space combat gameplay. Pre-orders are now available, with a collector's edition that includes a statue.

cards.headline: Fable releases in late February 2027 with Hayley Atwell as villain
cards.teaser: The upcoming Fable game has a release date and stars Marvel actor Hayley Atwell as the antagonist Isabel Hero of Wraithmarsh.
cards.body:
Microsoft confirmed that Fable will launch on February 23rd, 2027, following a delay from its original 2026 window. The company showcased new footage at its Xbox Games Showcase, revealing the game's villain: Isabel Hero of Wraithmarsh, portrayed by actress Hayley Atwell.

The reboot marks the first new entry in the fantasy RPG franchise since 2010's Fable III. Microsoft has announced additional cast members alongside the antagonist reveal, with a Premium Edition also available at launch.

hero.headline: Alexander Zverev wins French Open for first Grand Slam title
hero.body:
Alexander Zverev claimed his first Grand Slam title at the French Open, defeating Italian player Flavio Cobolli in a grueling five-set final. The second-seeded German won 6-1, 4-6, 6-4, 6-7 (5), 6-1 in what was described as an emotionally draining match that tested both players' mental fortitude.

The victory represents a breakthrough moment for Zverev after three previous Grand Slam final losses. Despite success at Masters 1000 events, the ATP Finals twice, and an Olympic gold medal in Tokyo 2020, the sport's biggest titles had eluded him until now. After the match concluded, Zverev dropped to his back and wept following Cobolli's missed overhead on the second championship point.

The French Open final unfolded as a tense affair across two weeks of a chaotic men's tournament. Zverev's path to the title became clearer when top seed Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic were eliminated in consecutive days, with Carlos Alcaraz absent due to injury. Cobolli, ranked 14th in the world, proved to be the only top-25 player Zverev faced in the draw.

Cobolli's journey to the final was unusual. He reached his first Grand Slam final without playing in the semifinals after his Italian compatriot Matteo Arnaldi withdrew due to illness. This meant the underdog felt the magnitude of the moment intensely from the start. He was completely outplayed in the opening set, winning just one game.

The match's second set saw Cobolli recover as he found his rhythm with the forehand and used his drop shot effectively. Zverev's familiar weaknesses emerged, particularly his forehand and second serve, which led to double faults at critical moments.

Zverev reasserted control in the third set, dominating on his serve while Cobolli managed only a 52% first-serve percentage and faced constant pressure. The fourth set became a turning point for the Italian, who recovered from down 5-4 to force a tiebreak. Cobolli's fighting spirit culminated in a running forehand winner that leveled the match at two sets each.

However, Cobolli's energy was depleted. He collapsed at the beginning of the fifth set, losing his opening service game and never recovering. Zverev closed out the match with conviction.

Addressing his team after winning, Zverev reflected on his journey: "We've been through injuries. We've been through heartbreak. We've been through losses. We've been losers at times in the important moments. But at the end of the day, we're grand slam champions now and that's what counts."

The victory also held special significance for Zverev at Roland Garros specifically. Four years earlier, he suffered a severe injury on the same court during a semifinal, leaving in a wheelchair with seven broken ligaments and two fractured bones. His return as champion represented a dramatic turnaround at a venue that held both his worst and best professional memories.

cards.headline: Denmark says Christian Eriksen conscious after collapsing during friendly against Ukraine
cards.teaser: Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during an international friendly but is now conscious, according to the Danish Football Association.
cards.body:
Christian Eriksen collapsed on the pitch during Denmark's friendly match against Ukraine on Sunday. The Danish Football Association confirmed that he regained consciousness and was attended to by medical staff in Odense before being taken from the field.

The incident prompted the referee to abandon the match. Eriksen, a former Tottenham and Manchester United midfielder, previously suffered cardiac arrest during a European Championship match in 2021.

cards.headline: Golden Knights edge Hurricanes in double overtime in Game 3 of Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights defeated the Carolina Hurricanes in double overtime in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final, one of the most dramatic games in finals history.
cards.body:
Shea Theodore scored at 5:38 of the second overtime to lift the Golden Knights past the Hurricanes 5-4 on Saturday night, giving Vegas a 2-1 series lead. Theodore's goal deflected off goalie Brandon Bussi's skate after the Golden Knights had squandered a four-goal lead.

The game featured a historic performance from Mitch Marner, who recorded the fastest hat trick in Stanley Cup Final history. Carolina's remarkable comeback nearly completed one of the most stunning reversals in championship history before falling short in the extended play.

cards.headline: Declan Rice named England vice-captain for World Cup
cards.teaser: Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice will serve as England's vice-captain at the upcoming World Cup.
cards.body:
Declan Rice has been appointed England's vice-captain for the World Cup by manager Thomas Tuchel. The Arsenal midfielder will serve as deputy to the captain as the team prepares for the tournament.

Tuchel recently played down the significance of Jude Bellingham wearing the armband during the second half of England's 1-0 warm-up victory against New Zealand, explaining that Bellingham wore it simply because he had the most international appearances among the players on the pitch at that time.

cards.headline: Tyrrell Hatton wins LIV Golf Andalucia by two strokes
cards.teaser: England's Tyrrell Hatton shot one-under par 70 in the final round to secure a two-shot victory at LIV Golf Andalucia.
cards.body:
Tyrrell Hatton claimed the title at LIV Golf Andalucia with a final round of 70, finishing one-under par. The English golfer maintained his lead to win by two strokes over the field.

The victory adds another title to Hatton's resume in the LIV Golf series. His steady final round allowed him to hold off challengers and secure the championship in Spain.

cards.headline: Keely Hodgkinson sets personal best but finishes second to Audrey Werro at Diamond League
cards.teaser: Olympic 800m champion Keely Hodgkinson ran a personal best time at the Diamond League meet in Stockholm but was beaten by Audrey Werro.
cards.body:
Keely Hodgkinson set a new personal best at the Diamond League event in Stockholm, but Switzerland's Audrey Werro claimed victory in the women's 800 meters. Werro's winning time of 1:53.98 represents the third fastest in history.

Despite the defeat, Hodgkinson's performance marked a significant achievement as the Olympic champion ran faster than ever before. The result underscores the competitive strength of the women's 800 meters at the highest level of international athletics.

cards.headline: Lewis Hamilton finishes second at Monaco Grand Prix
cards.teaser: Lewis Hamilton placed second at the Monaco Grand Prix and said he feels like he is reminding people of his abilities.
cards.body:
Lewis Hamilton finished second at the Monaco Grand Prix, as Kimi Antonelli claimed victory in a dramatic race. The event featured two safety car periods and a red flag before its chaotic conclusion.

The result at the prestigious Monte Carlo circuit highlighted Hamilton's continued competitive form with Mercedes on one of Formula One's most challenging street circuits.

hero.headline: Scott Pelley Says Bari Weiss Wanted 60 Minutes to Misrepresent Police Shooting
hero.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran correspondent at 60 Minutes, publicly criticized CBS News leadership during a staff meeting on Monday morning, targeting the network's recent personnel decisions and the editorial direction set by editor-in-chief Bari Weiss.

The confrontation followed CBS News's Thursday announcement that it had fired the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. During the Monday meeting with newly appointed executive producer Nick Bilton and managing editor Charles Forelle, Pelley launched a direct attack on Weiss's management of the program.

"She's murdering 60 Minutes," Pelley said, according to sources familiar with the situation. "She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that." Pelley also criticized how the network handled the firing of executive producer Tanya Simon. When managing editor Forelle accused Pelley of being rude, Pelley responded that the network itself had been rude in its treatment of Simon.

The staff meeting revealed significant internal discord at the network. Bilton told Pelley that he would not be "intimidated" by his remarks, while staff members present gave Pelley a standing ovation in apparent support of his position. CBS News declined to comment on the meeting.

The tensions at 60 Minutes reflect broader concerns about editorial independence and journalistic integrity. In a statement released Wednesday, Alfonsi, who had reported a segment about a prison in El Salvador that was shelved by Weiss, stated: "The wall between editorial independence and corporate interest at CBS is being methodically torn down." She added that "journalists willing to challenge authority are being pushed aside in favor of those who will not."

Vega suggested that political bias was influencing editorial decisions. "In recent months, my producing teams and I have experienced efforts to insert political bias into our stories," she said. "Reporting teams have held back on submitting story pitches about important news topics out of fear of the internal repercussions." She called this "censorship, both imposed and self-driven" that is "dangerous for the show and dangerous for democracy." The network disputed Vega's characterization.

Despite the turmoil, some veteran correspondents have indicated they plan to remain with the show. Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and Jon Wertheim have said they will stay, though questions persist about the program's future composition and direction.

Pelley's public criticism represents an unusual departure from typical network news protocol, where such disputes are usually handled privately. According to sources, CBS News has made overtures to Pelley, recognizing his importance to the show, though the exchange raises questions about his long-term future at 60 Minutes.

cards.headline: Dua Lipa and Callum Turner Marry in Sicily
cards.teaser: The pop star and actor held a wedding ceremony in Sicily, with Elton John performing at the event.
cards.body:
Dua Lipa and actor Callum Turner married in a ceremony in Sicily, marking their second wedding celebration. The couple had previously held a secret wedding in London before the Sicilian event. Elton John serenaded the couple with his song Your Song during the Sicilian celebration.

The wedding in Palermo reportedly divided local opinion, with some residents questioning the disruption caused by the high-profile event. The starry ceremony drew attention for its location and guest list, making it one of the more prominent celebrity weddings of the year.

cards.headline: Bob Dylan Performs Basement Tapes Song for First Time in 14 Years
cards.teaser: Dylan played You Ain't Goin' Nowhere during a concert, two days after performing another rare Basement Tapes track.
cards.body:
Bob Dylan recently performed "You Ain't Goin' Nowhere," a song from the Basement Tapes, for the first time in 14 years. The performance took place two days after Dylan played "Baby, Won't You Be My Baby" live for the first time since recording it 59 years ago.

The Basement Tapes are a collection of recordings Dylan made in 1967 with The Band. These performances highlight Dylan's return to material from his catalog that he rarely plays in concert.

cards.headline: Ariana Grande Opens Eternal Sunshine Tour in Oakland
cards.teaser: The singer performed the opening show of her Eternal Sunshine Tour at Oakland Arena.
cards.body:
Ariana Grande opened her Eternal Sunshine Tour at Oakland Arena on Saturday night. The performance earned praise for showcasing her vocal prowess and commanding stage presence.

The tour supports her latest album and marks her return to large-scale touring venues. The Oakland show demonstrated what fans can expect as the tour moves to additional cities.

cards.headline: New Spyro Game Announced for Spring 2027 Release
cards.teaser: The first new Spyro game in nearly two decades will feature the franchise's first dragon-flight mechanic.
cards.body:
Toys for Bob is developing a new Spyro game titled Spyro: A Realm Beyond, launching in spring 2027 across Xbox, PlayStation 5, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2. This marks the first original Spyro title since 2008. Tom Kenny, who voiced the character in the original games, returns to voice the redesigned purple dragon.

The game introduces a significant new mechanic: players can take flight at any time during gameplay. Creative director Lou Studdert emphasized this core feature, explaining that players will dive to build speed, use fire-breath to create updrafts, and manage their wings strategically—fully embracing the capabilities of being a dragon.

cards.headline: Vincent Cassel to Play Napoleon in Video Game Valor Mortis
cards.teaser: The White Lotus star will voice Napoleon Bonaparte in the upcoming first-person game.
cards.body:
Vincent Cassel, who will appear in the fourth season of The White Lotus, has been cast as Napoleon Bonaparte in the video game Valor Mortis. The first-person Soulslike game is set in a supernatural reimagining of 19th-century Europe.

Players will take on the role of William, a resurrected soldier of the Grande Armée. The game blends historical settings with supernatural elements, offering an alternate take on the Napoleonic era.

cards.headline: Morgan Wallen Cancels Pittsburgh Show Over Weather Concerns
cards.teaser: The country singer called off a concert citing safety concerns about his stage setup, though severe weather did not materialize.
cards.body:
Morgan Wallen canceled his Pittsburgh concert due to forecasted adverse weather conditions. He explained that his large stage setup posed a safety risk to attendees in the predicted weather, potentially becoming fatal. However, the severe weather he cited did not materialize as expected.

Wallen addressed criticism surrounding the cancellation, defending his decision to prioritize safety. The incident generated disappointment among fans who had traveled to attend the show.

hero.headline: Trump to press Netanyahu against retaliating for Iranian missile attack
hero.body:
President Trump said he will call Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to urge him not to retaliate after Iran launched ballistic missiles at northern Israel on Sunday, threatening a ceasefire the administration has worked to broker. Trump told Axios he would press Netanyahu to stand down, saying both sides have now struck each other and further escalation is unnecessary.

The Iranian attack marked the first such strike in two months and came after Israel struck Beirut earlier. The Israeli Defense Forces confirmed multiple waves of ballistic missiles were fired at northern Israel. A U.S. official told NewsNation that Trump has been briefed on the incident. The attack raised immediate concerns about the fragility of the ceasefire arrangement between the United States and Iran.

Trump framed the situation as a cycle both countries need to end. He told Axios that Israel had conducted its strike and Iran had now responded, characterizing the exchanges as both sides having their opportunity to act. The president indicated he sees no need for another round of attacks and hopes to preserve prospects for a lasting peace deal in the region.

The strikes threaten to derail ongoing efforts to negotiate a broader agreement aimed at ending the conflict. Diplomats have worked for weeks to establish terms that could hold, but the Sunday night attack underscored how quickly tensions can reignite. The timing comes as the Trump administration approaches the 18-month mark of its second term, with Middle East policy remaining a central focus.

Former national security adviser John Bolton warned separately that Trump's handling of the Iran situation could trigger nuclear proliferation in the Middle East. Bolton wrote in an opinion piece that contradictory decisions during the conflict have created conditions for a potential arms race, regardless of whatever deal the administration ultimately reaches with Tehran. The administration now faces the immediate task of preventing further escalation while trying to keep diplomatic channels open.

cards.headline: Senate passes immigration enforcement funding bill
cards.teaser: The Senate approved major immigration enforcement funding legislation, sending the measure to the House for consideration.
cards.body:
The Senate passed a significant immigration enforcement funding bill, marking progress for Trump administration deportation priorities. The legislation now moves to the House of Representatives for consideration.

Lawmakers face additional immigration-related decisions in the coming days, including the future of a surveillance program set to expire next week. The bill represents a victory for the administration's enforcement agenda, though further legislative battles loom.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
cards.teaser: Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland secured the Democratic nomination in New Mexico's gubernatorial primary.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served as Interior Secretary in the Biden administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. The victory positions her for a potential historic outcome in the general election.

If elected in November, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in United States history. She previously served in Congress representing New Mexico before joining Biden's cabinet.

cards.headline: House Democrats plan investigations of Trump administration officials
cards.teaser: Democratic lawmakers are preparing investigations and potential prosecutions of Trump officials if they retake power in 2029.
cards.body:
House Democrats have outlined plans to investigate Trump administration officials for alleged legal violations across multiple areas if they regain control of Congress. The targets include actions related to immigration raids, strikes on alleged drug boats, financial dealings, and use of prosecutorial power against political opponents.

Democrats have accused top members of the president's team of breaking laws throughout the administration's tenure. The party views 2029 as a potential opportunity to hold officials accountable through congressional oversight and possible criminal referrals, though such plans depend on electoral outcomes.

cards.headline: Maine Democrats consider Electoral College retaliation if Nebraska changes rules
cards.teaser: Democratic candidates for Maine governor signaled support for changing how the state awards electoral votes if Nebraska adopts winner-take-all.
cards.body:
Democrats in Maine are threatening to alter how the state awards Electoral College votes if Republican-led Nebraska changes its system for the 2028 presidential election. Several Democratic gubernatorial candidates have indicated they would back adopting a winner-take-all approach if Nebraska makes similar changes.

The potential moves represent escalating election politics that could influence the 2028 presidential race. Currently, both Maine and Nebraska split their electoral votes by congressional district rather than awarding all votes to the statewide winner, a system unique to the two states.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Hilton and Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Early returns in California's gubernatorial primary show Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra ahead in their respective party races.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading in California's primary election to determine a successor to Gov. Gavin Newsom. The race features several prominent candidates from both parties vying for their party's nomination.

Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer are also competing in the race, while Republican Chad Bianco is running alongside Hilton. The primary will determine which candidates advance to the general election to lead California, the nation's most populous state.

cards.headline: Top Democrat calls Pulte appointment to intelligence role dangerous
cards.teaser: Rep. Jim Himes labeled the selection of Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence the most dangerous Trump appointment.
cards.body:
Rep. Jim Himes, the ranking Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, criticized President Trump's decision to name Federal Housing Finance Agency head Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence. Himes called it the worst and most dangerous appointment made by the president.

Several lawmakers from both parties have objected to the appointment. Himes joins bipartisan voices expressing concern about Pulte's qualifications and suitability for overseeing the intelligence community.
